title.narrative: SKL International - Förstudie om decentralisering i DRC
SKL International - PreStudy on decentralisation in DRC

description.narrative:
SKL International har ansökt till Sveriges ambassad i Kinshasa för att finansiera en förstudie i Demokratiska republiken Kongo (DRC) för att öka deras förståelse för decentraliseringsprocessen, det politiska landskapet mellan provinsiell förvaltning och centralregering, för att identifiera möjligheter för Sverige och kontextualisera sina tidigare erfarenheter och drar slutsatser för framtida insatser.
Förstudien förväntas ta sex månader och den totala budgeten, inklusive programchef, personal och controller samt två månaders uppdrag i DRC, är 2 575 800 SEK.

The SKL International has applied to the Embassy of Sweden in Kinshasa for funding a pre-study in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to increase their understanding on decentralization process, the policy landscape between provincial administrative governance and central government, identify possible opportunity for Sweden to add it values and contextualize their previous experiences and draw conclusions for future interventions to support the fragile devolvement.
The pre-study is expected to take six months and the total budget, including programme manager, staff and controller as well as two-month long mission in DRC, is 2 575 800 SEK.

The objective of the pre-study is to provide an analytical and situational overview of the current situation in the DRC in terms of the decentralization process and local self-governance as well as to propose and describe suitable interventions for a programme in support of decentralization efforts in the DRC from 2021 and onwards.
The pre-study shall enquire the ideas of interventions to i) support provincial State institutions to strengthen their administration; ii) support administration governance programme ; and iii) identify opportunity and interest in pushing for reforms.

sector.narrative: Decentralisation and support to subnational government

description.narrative: The partner visited DRC on a few occassions during the implementation period. They travelled to a few selected provinces to assess the needs for support and the possiblities to develop a project that would meet the needs found. Based on the findings during the visits, the partner developed a full range programme. The partner has also become active in donor corodination groups and are liaising with other organisations in the same field, notably UDCDF and the EU.
